title: Three entry points, three different vocabularies for the same failure - one of them raw Dart exception text
what_happened: The same underlying condition - 'the address you gave me does not answer' - is reported three different ways depending on which button the user pressed. Enter IP: 'Cannot reach http://192.0.2.77:8080/api/info from this device.' followed by two well-written paragraphs of what to check on the PC and on the phone. Relay: 'Could not reach the relay: SocketException: Failed host lookup: \'relay.tail1a2b3.invalid\' (OS Error: No address associated with hostname, errno = 7)'. Tailscale: the wrong message entirely (see the P1 above). The relay text leaks a Dart exception class, an OS error string and an errno onto a consumer screen at 2am.
expected: One shared reachability-failure renderer used by every entry point: what was tried (scheme://host:port/api/info), the plain-language cause (name not found / connection refused / timed out), and the next step. The Enter-IP copy is already the right answer - promote it and delete the other two paths' bespoke strings.
repro: Compare Enter IP -> 192.0.2.77 -> Connect, Connect via Relay -> https://relay.tail1a2b3.invalid + abcd-efgh-ijkl -> Connect, and Connect over Tailscale -> skotiq-rig.tail1a2b3.ts.net -> Connect.

title: After discovery has already failed, the biggest button on screen re-runs the thing that just failed
what_happened: The connection screen offers seven actions. Six are equally-weighted low-contrast text buttons (Enter IP 209x126px, Scan QR 216x126px, Connect over Tailscale, Connect via Relay, Saved servers, Skip Connection) and exactly one is a filled primary button: 'Search for Server' (996x131px), which repeats the automatic discovery that ran on launch and failed 4 seconds ago. The action with the highest success probability for someone standing next to their rig - Scan QR, because the desktop puts a QR on screen when you start pairing - is a small text button, and the error card that lists 'Scanning the QR code from the desktop' as the first thing to try offers no button to do it.
expected: Once discovery has failed at least once, promote 'Scan QR' to the primary filled button and demote 'Search for Server' to a text action ('Scan again'). Better still, make the three bullets in the failure card tappable so 'Scanning the QR code from the desktop' opens the scanner directly - that removes a full step from the most likely recovery path.
repro: Launch with no appliance, wait for the failure card, count the actions and their weights.

title: The Tailscale sheet tells the user to go install an app but will not take them there, and never checks whether it is already installed
what_happened: Step 1 of the sheet reads 'Install Tailscale on this phone - Get it from the App Store / Play Store and sign in with the same account as your observatory PC.' It is plain text: nothing is tappable, so the user must leave Skotiq, find the store, search for Tailscale, install, sign in, and come back and retype everything (which the sheet then discards on the next failure). The sheet also never checks whether Tailscale is present or up on this phone, even though that is trivially detectable on Android and is the single most common reason the connect will fail.
expected: On a phone this should be a button that deep-links to the Play Store listing (market://details?id=com.tailscale.ipn), and step 1 should collapse to a green tick when the package is already installed. Detecting 'Tailscale is not installed' before the connect attempt turns a mystery timeout into a one-line answer.
repro: Connection screen -> Connect over Tailscale -> read step 1; nothing in it is a control.

title: Manual entry asks for an 'Access Token' that a first-time user cannot have, and never mentions the port it will use
what_happened: The Enter-IP form has exactly two fields: 'Server address' and 'Access Token' (with a show/hide eye). A first-run user has no access token - the real first-connect credential is the pairing CODE, which the app asks for afterwards in its own dialog. There is no helper text saying the token is optional, and no hint that the address may include a port or that 8080 is assumed; the user only learns the port from the failure message afterwards ('Cannot reach http://192.0.2.77:8080/api/info').
expected: Label it 'Access token (optional - leave blank to pair with a code)', exactly the phrasing the Tailscale sheet already uses for the same field ('Leave blank to pair with a code'), and give the address field the hint '192.168.1.20 or 192.168.1.20:8080 (default 8080)'.
repro: Connection screen -> Enter IP -> inspect the two fields.
